_note: Amiga Phantasie III art (tools/scripts/extract_amiga_p3_graphics.py; formats in reverse-engineering/amiga/phantasie3/FORMAT.md; the extract keeps a copy as pack.json, pinned by a test). Paths are relative to root. The overworld is drawn from phantasy.set's 250 tiles of 16x16 (tile = map byte, a 9x9 window as the Amiga, 0x9b92; the party is tile 89 OR-ed over its cell, 0x378a), over the DOS grid the remaster plays (54 Scandor cells differ, 13 of them in terrain; FORMAT.md section 4). The dungeon map is one 8x5 dng.csh glyph per cell (0x1e47a/0x1e750): dungeon_cells are [min, max, glyph] by map byte, other bytes the default; a cell not yet seen draws dungeon_unseen. Monster pictures by record byte 27 (0x1b4c8; Wolf and Mud Elemental get none cut: the Amiga shows the earlier fight's rank-1 picture, or hangs on the first fight after boot (FORMAT.md 6, 8.8); the remaster gives them borrowed pictures, D3-067: Wolf the Wild Dog's, Mud Elemental the party elemental's, heros 22), portraits by race (table 0x239a0; files named by the remaster race id, the elemental is portrait.elemental, picture 22), both shown in the heros.cmp palette as the combat screen loads it (0x19906); colour 0 is opaque (plain blits). Scroll IV (item 126) is the picture D/s6. Text uses the remaster font (the Amiga's is the system font, not on the disk [~]). Each PNG holds its own screen's colours, so no palette is forced on the frame. palettes.astral is D/W2.cmp's, in force while the party-defeat scene prints (0x1dc16): its text is colour 15, an undead fate colour 14.
name: Amiga

tile_maps._past_map: The Amiga's view may run one column past a map (Scandor and the Netherworld; FORMAT.md section 4): it reads the bytes after the map, so a column past the east edge shows the next row's first cell. [region, index, tile] are bytes the code itself writes there: the Netherworld's 496 and 497 := 0xF9 (0x1ec62). Any other byte past a map is undefined memory and draws black.
tile_maps._view_counters: [region, columns, rows]: the size counters 0x24098 / 0x24096 the overworld view and step test run on, as the plane change 0x1eb18 sets them (FORMAT.md section 4). The boot runs 0x1eb18 with plane 0 after a previous plane of 1 (0x76ce / 0x76fa / 0x7758), so Scandor's are 50 x 74 from the start, not the 75 rows phantasy.set gives (s125 [C], seen on FS-UAE: at row 73 with the view on rows 66-74 a step north does not scroll). The view's centre stops at counter - 4: Scandor shows columns 42-50 (one past the map) and rows 66-74; the Netherworld 31 x 15 columns 23-31 and rows 7-15. Light / Dark (9 x 8, the 9x9 plane) always show the whole plane.

town_screen._note: Doors (s102, 0xacc8): on going into a building the 48x48 street rect is saved, the open door from D/w3 copied over it, 15 ticks waited, the street restored (FORMAT.md section 3, D/w3). Positions from table 0x23070. The tick is taken as 1/50 s (Delay) [~].
town_screen._name: Name (0x7e54): 12 cells from text cell 14, the name at cell 14 + (12 - len) / 2, so an odd gap sits half a cell left of the exact centre. Towns 16-17 (Dark, Death): the street fades to the dim palette 0x23050 instead of 0x24010 (= the picture's own, palettes.map) and the name pen is 0 (0x78ee, 0xb228); 0x4390 is the palette fade (FORMAT.md section 3).

body_figure._note: 0x9694 (called by the party roster 0x93e0 for every member whose status, record +0x2c, is not Dead): pieces in draw order at 0x220da (x bytes * 8, y); 0x95f8 swaps the arm and leg words first, so the viewer's left is the character's right. Shape 16 + 7 * state + piece for Okay / Injured / Broken; Gone fills the clear rectangle (0x648, inclusive x .. x + 8, or x + 24 for the fifth piece, rows y .. y + 7) in colour 0. The chest (piece 6) is always shape 22. The masked blit 0x2ce4 keeps colour 0 transparent.

scroll_frame._note: 0x1e2c2 (text scrolls 0x1f7e2, and two other text pages): fill (8,8)-(312,192) inclusive in colour 4, text in colour 2 from (8, 8); the frame on the first page only, 40 columns of 8-px scroll.csh pieces (0x1e838 draws the left 8 px): top row corners 54 / 55, else 58 + rnd mod 3; bottom row (y 192) corners 57 / 56, else 61 + rnd and 1; rows 1..23 left 63 + rnd mod 3, right 66 + rnd mod 3. Colours 4 / 2 of the map palette.

keep_windows._note: FORMAT.md 2.3: the keep questions are OK / CANCEL windows (52-B structs at 0x23228, drawn by 0x3904 in the map palette 0x24010). Box filled (0x648, inclusive) in colour +4 = 0; frame 0x31e6 in colours +0 = 4 (outer: top y0 and left x0 to x1 - 1 / y1 - 1) and +2 = 3 (inner, one pixel in and down: to x1 / y1); text colour 9. dungeon = window 1, op 6 'Keep ...?' (0x1cb26): box (0, 72)-(319, 140), the question at text cell (1, 10); fight = window 23, the fight find (0x1a044, two buttons forced at 0x1a048): box (16, 64)-(300, 128), the finder and item at cell (4, 9), 'Will the party keep it?' at (6, 11). Buttons 64x18 from dlgbttns.cmp, x in bytes * 8; the second state while held (0x15ea). Keys (0x3ba0): Return / O = OK, C = CANCEL, a click on a button.
keep_windows._note_s125: s125 [C] seen (FS-UAE, parity/shots/p3-amiga-keep-dungeon*.png): 0x3904 loads the map palette only while 0x24070 = 0, and the dungeon (which fades to dng.csh's palette 0x244de at 0x1bd72) leaves it 1, so every window drawn in a dungeon (window 1's 'Keep Scroll II?', 'An exit. Will you take it?'; by the code also a dungeon fight's reward and find windows, after 0x1da5c's fade back) shows in the dungeon palette. Its indices 0, 3, 4, 9 (fill, frame, text) equal the map's; the buttons' label (index 8) is #FFFF00, not #FFDB49, and held (index 5) #00DBFF, not #24B692. button_palette = the palette the button art is cut in; dungeon_palette = the one its indices show in while the party is in a dungeon.
keep_windows._note_s117: s117: the town's Bank is window 9 (its text pointer set to 'The party is in the bank...' at 0x7464), Trade's 'Whose item shall be traded?' / 'Who gets the item?' window 6 and 'Trade which item?' window 10: boxes and OK / CANCEL (bytes x 8) from the window table at DATA 0x23228 [C]; the trade windows: 0x127ce(64 / 65) draws window 6, 0xf2c0 window 10 [C] (s156). Text origins measured on the s116 captures, and s156 read in the code to the same values [C] (FORMAT.md 8.2): bank title, the gold / bank labels, the value column, the two picks (or 'How much:'); trade title, then one row per member or item, 8 px apart. list_colours: map palette 4 (tan: labels, rows) and 8 (yellow: values, the picked row), as captured.
keep_windows._note_s118: s118: the combat orders screen's rank question (0x19806) is window 20 (0x23638: box (24, 72)-(296, 136), title cell (4, 10) colour 9, OK / CANCEL at bytes (10, 111) / (23, 111)) [C]; 0x19806 sets its text pointer to '\r     Target rank 1? (or 2)' (0x231fc), so the line starts 5 cells in on the row under the title cell. OK = rank 1, CANCEL = rank 2 (0x19878: the order + 11, Cast 16).
keep_windows._note_s119: s119: the orders screen's Cast opens the spell window 11 (0xf770, struct 0x23464: box (56, 24)-(252, 176), no title, buttons OK / CANCEL / MORE at bytes (8, 151) / (16, 151) / (24, 151), keys -1 / 'C' / 'M'; the button count +26 is set to 3 when the caster knows more than 12 spells, else 2, so MORE shows only then) [C]. 'Select' at cell (8, 4), the name at 15, "'s spell:" after it, colour 8. The list 0xff82: the known spells (record +0xb0, sorted highest id first by 0xd08c), 12 a page from row 6, name at column 8 and the MP cost at 27 (0xab1c), colour 4, the cursor row 8. The heal target (spells 1-4) is window 6 (0x127ce(33), struct 0x23360: the Trade windows' box), 'Who shall be healed in combat?' at cell (5, 7) colour 8, one member a row from row 9 (0x12ac8): name 2, race 10, level 21, class 24, status 32, colour 4, the cursor row 8. Both lists: '8' / Up up, '2' / Down down (wrapping), a press on a row moves the cursor there (0x17a6), Return / O / OK takes it, C / CANCEL = Thrust (0x19656); M / MORE the next page (back to the first after the last).
keep_windows._note_s120: s120 (FORMAT.md 8.5) [C]: M and H on the fight's field. Both are drawn by 0x3904 with the combat palette in force (0x198a2 sets 0x2445e and 0x24070 = 1, so 0x3904 keeps it), no buttons (+46 = -1), then 0x1e8c4(1) waits for any key or mouse button and 0x274a puts back what was under the window. Colours are combat-palette indices. monster_names = 0x1a264(1): window 23 with +8 / +12 set to 128 / 191 (box (16, 128)-(300, 191)), its frame +0 / +2 set to 2 / 7 and its buttons +26 to 0 (all put back after); 'Monster Identification:' at cell (7, 18) colour 1 on 0; then 0x1a44c(rank, count, 1) for rank 2 (struct 0x2481e) and rank 1 (0x24794) when the count (+2) > 0 and the id (+0) >= 0: 'Rank  :' at column 7 on row 22 - rank, the rank's digit at 12 (0xab1c), the count at 15, the name (0x241dc + 38 id, trailing blanks cut, '(s)' put after) at 17. text = title, then rank 1's 'Rank', digit, ':', count, name. party_health = 0xadac: window 24 (0x23708: box (24, 16)-(286, 199), frame 2 / 7, fill 0); its title (+22, set at 0x7482 to 0x23178 'Name:\rStatus:\rHits:\rMagic:\rHead:\rLt Arm:\rRt Arm:\rTorso:\rLt Leg:\rRt Leg:') at cell (4, 3) colour 1; one column a member (0x240e0 less a summoned elemental, 0x24124) by 0xae2c(slot): slots 0-2 at columns 12 / 20 / 28 row 3, slots 3-5 the same columns row 14, and slot 3 first prints the labels again at (4, 14) colour 1. A member: name (+0) colour 4; row + 1 the status 0x22eec[+0x2c] (Dead, Okay, Asleep, Out, Down) colour 15; row + 2 HP current (+0x22) right-aligned to column + 2 (0xabec), ':' at + 3, the most (+0x20) at + 4; row + 3 the same for MP (+0x1e, +0x1c), colour 15; rows + 4 to + 9 the six areas +0xf2..+0xfc (Head, Lt Arm, Rt Arm, Torso, Lt Leg, Rt Leg) as Okay / Injured / Broken / Gone (0x22edc..0x22ee8) in colour 15 / 14 / 13 / 12. text = labels, labels again, slots 0-5; colours = labels, name, values, then Okay, Injured, Broken, Gone.
keep_windows._note_s134: s134 [C] static: the message box 0xaaac(text) puts the text in window 7's title (+22, 0x233aa) and draws window 7 (struct 0x23394) through 0x3904 with save flag 1 (what lies under is put back after). Struct: frame +0 / +2 = 4 / 3, fill +4 = 0, box (0, 0)-(319, 52), title cell (1, 1) in colour +18 = 8 on +20 = 0 (map palette 8, yellow; a '\r' goes one row down at the title column, 0x854), one button (+26 = 1) slot 1 = OK at bytes (9, 27) = x 72, y 27, its key +46 = 0. With key 0, 0x3ba0 ends the wait on any key (0x3c2a clears its loop flag for every non-zero key) or a click on OK. No sound (0xaae2, the window-1 message, plays sound 36 first). 78 callers: the combat Cast refusals (0x19430...), the town / guild refusals ('The party is not assembled.' ...), the spells cast outside a fight, the disk messages. On the orders screen the palette in force is the map's (0x24070 = 1, s128), so the text is #FFDB49.
keep_windows._note_s135: s135 [C] static: the 78 callers of 0xaaac (FORMAT.md 8.4, the message box caller table). text_ids = the remaster lines whose Amiga equivalent goes through window 7 outside the orders screen, shown in window 7 under AMIGA SCREENS: the guild Add refusals (0xd100: 0xd12a not assembled, 0xd15a an elemental is in the party, 0xd180 this character is in the party, 0xd210 the party has 6 characters), Purge of a party member (0xb54a), the roster full (0xb4b6), the inn the party cannot afford (0x8264) and the trade's cannot carry (0xf5be). The text is the remaster's line; formatted lines (picks the lock, disarms the trap, the monster level) are not matched.
keep_windows._note_s158: s158 [C] static (FORMAT.md 8.4, the town dispatch 0xb1cc read key by key; DOS guild_menu root 0xac21 the same): text_ids gain III's own lines for the remaster refusals whose condition matches one for one: guild.roster_empty (Add with an empty roster, S408), core.p3.cannot_train (S417: Dead / Out, Undead or level 21, DOS item 1), core.guild.learn_cant_afford (DOS ovl2 0x1d12 / Amiga 0x1068a: party gold below the cost), cast.x_knows_no_spells (a caster with no spell known: S443, Amiga 0x84e0 / 0xb8aa), useitem.x_carries_nothing (Use Item by a member with no item: S416, Amiga 0xba7c); the remaster's empty-party Drop / Learn / Training lines now read S405 "The party is not assembled.", already listed.
keep_windows._note_s140: s140 [C] static: File > Info (the bar outside the towns, key ? or /, 0x83e0 to 0x86e6; the town's File > Info 0xb25a calls it too) draws window 0 (struct 0x23228) through 0x3904 with save flag 1 (what lies under is put back after): frame +0 / +2 = 4 / 3, fill +4 = 0, box (36, 44)-(284, 168), title cell (5, 7) in colour +18 = 9 on +20 = 0 (#FF9224 in the map palette; the dungeon's index 9 is the same), the title = pointer 0x2308c (set at 0x7450 into +22) = the credits, ten rows split by CR (0x854: one row down at the title column; the leading blanks are 8-px cells), one button (+26 = 1) slot 1 = OK at bytes (10, 143) = x 80, y 143, its key +46 = 'O', +48 = 0. 0x3ba0 with a key: O, o, Return or a click on OK (0x13ee writes +46) end the wait with 1, c (or the second key 0) with 0; every other key is read and dropped. 0x3904 keeps the palette in force (0x24070 = 1), so in a dungeon the window shows in dng.csh's palette (the OK label yellow #FFFF00, s125). text_ids[0] = the credits string.
keep_windows._note_s141: s141 [C] static and seen (FS-UAE, FORMAT.md 8.9): Options > Party Status (P outside the towns, 0x83e0 to 0x8832) counts the found items, draws window 22 (struct 0x236a0) through 0x3904 with save flag 1 (frame 4 / 3, fill 0, box (72, 28)-(248, 180), one OK at bytes (12, 155)), prints the labels (pointer 0x23160) with 0x854 at cell (10, 5) and the values with 0xab54 / 0xab1c at column 23, rows 7 / 8 / 9 (days out = the thirds counter 0x25d46 / 3, the experience pool 0x25d3e, the purse 0x25d42) and 12-18 (the counts), all in colour 5 of the palette in force (map #24B692 outside, dungeon #00DBFF below), then waits as the credits do (0x3ba0 'O'). kinds = 0x885e's compares over the found-item list 0x25cc4 (count 0x25d3c): 1-20 Shields, 21-40 Armour, 41-60 Bows, 61-100 Weapons, 101-120 Potions, 121-140 Scrolls, 141 and up Treasure (one number: no upper bound). Seen with poked ids: counts 1-7, every boundary held. font: both windows' text is topaz 8 (the screen font 0x854 draws with; window 22's 'Days out:' matched the ROM glyphs pixel for pixel), so each character fills the Amiga's 8-px cell.
keep_windows._note_s156: s156 [C] static (FORMAT.md 8.5 / 8.9 'The bars as pack data'): the game's own menu bars, the places 0x12d6 computes once a list at start-up (0x7700-0x772e: the lists 0x238a4 town, 0x23910 outside the towns, 0x2397c the fight), written out: a title at text column c is drawn at x (c + 1) * 8, text top y 2 (0x1c5c: Move(x, 8), topaz 8), the next title at c + its length + 2; pulled down (0x184a) the title's cells c ... c + length + 1 are inverted over rows 1-10 (highlight), the box (0x28de) starts at column c rounded down to even, y 12, its width the widest item's length + 1 rounded up to even, its height (items + 1) * 8, solid pen 15 and no frame (frame: false); items through 0x854 at the box column + 1 (item_x), rows y 16 + 8 i, pen 0 on 15; the pointer's row inverts the box's full width over 8 rows. The bar 0x3894: rows 0-10 in pen 15, titles pen 0 (the open one 15 on 0). Pens are indices of the palette in force: the combat palette on the field, the map's (or the dungeon's) outside the towns, the map's in a town (w4) and town_dim's in the dim towns 16-17. Items and their keys: the key table 0x2189c (15 bytes a menu: town rows 0-2, outside 3-5, fight 6-8; byte 0 = the title, 0 = no key; the '-----' rule rows have key 0). actions name what each item does in the remaster (the fight's and outside's are checked against CombatPresenter.AmigaFieldMenus / AmigaOutsideBar.Menus by the tests).

title_sequence._note: The Amiga boot (reverse-engineering/amiga/phantasie3/FORMAT.md 'Title'): 0x736c unpacks Graphics/Title.cmp to the screen, starts the tune D/M0 (0x1fa5c reads 830 bytes, three voices on Paula 0-2, a VBL interrupt driver 0x2192: 2897 VBLs, 48.3 s at the NTSC 60 Hz [~]; FORMAT.md 7.1), which plays on while the game loads, sets the title palette, loads the rest of the game's files and clears the screen (0x7660) with no key read [C]. The manual: 'the title page will be displayed. Hit any key to get to the Initial Menu' [X]; the remaster waits for a key as the manual says (D3-065). plays_on (s157, user): the tune is not stopped with the splash; it plays on into the game (live s156: about 28 s over the Initial Menu when no key is pressed, capture_s156_p3_title.md) until its end or the first sound effect, whose driver start 0x1f52 (0xb126, FORMAT.md 7.2) resets every voice [C].

reward_scene._note: The gods' reward (root 0x1ee82; FORMAT.md 2.4, 3.1) [C] s109. Intro: on the cleared screen, still in the dungeon palette 0x244de that 0x1da5c set after the fight (0x1db8e; the keep windows' 0x3904 sets the map palette only while 0x24070 = 0, and the fight left it 1 at 0x19914), the line 'You hear noises...' then 0x1f30a(1): 50 flashes 0x1b814 at x = rnd mod 36 + rnd mod 3 (max 36) bytes, y = rnd mod 120 + rnd mod 22 + 6; shapes 37, 38, 39 drawn over each other, each followed by 0x2af6(w) = w + 1 VBLs; w (0x241e8) starts at 7 and goes 1 down every 5 flashes (from flash 0) to 1; then 'When the noises...' and 0x1f30a(0): the same, w 1 up every 5 to 8. Sound 15 (0xb126(15), sound_effects) starts before each flash's second frame (sound_frame 1); each start cuts the one before (the driver start 0x1f52 resets all three voices), so the noise grows with the speed (s110). Tune D/M1 (659 B) starts once the picture and 'Press a key' are drawn (0x1efe8) and is stopped at the scene's end (0x1f24a); it does not loop. No key is read during the intro (the remaster's Return skips a run). VBL rate 60 Hz (NTSC) [~], as the title tune.

combat_flash._note: The flash 0x1b814 as a fight's spell effect (FORMAT.md 2.4) [C] static s110. damage_monster 0x1833e flashes the monster hit when its flag (+18) is set: the party's spells (0x181b8, 0x182c6, 0x186f6); its melee (0x16230) passes 0. damage_character 0x17e16 flashes the member when its flag (+12) is set: the monsters' Fireflash (0x1673e), Sleep (0x17bc2, 0 damage), armour / attack lowered (0x17d56, 0 damage), Mindblast / Fireball / breath (0x17c80, 0x176c2) and the stunning / draining touches (0x177c8 types 34 / 35); a plain melee hit passes 0 ('hits!' with sound 15, no flash). Speed word 0x241e8 = 6 in a fight (boot 0x7656, back after the reward scene 0x1f13a): 7 VBLs a frame, 21 a flash, sound 15 before frame 1. Member: x = max(0, 6 slot - 1) + rnd mod 3 + 2 (max 36) bytes, y = 140 + rnd mod 22 + 6; its portrait at (48 slot, 143 / 138 / 133 by record +8 = Back / Middle / Front, 0x1b42e). Monster: its own picture's x + rnd mod 3 (+2 for a giant), y + rnd mod 22 + 6 (0x1b150 / 0x1b4c8). Shapes 37-39 in the combat palette (heros.cmp's, 0x19906): red, orange, yellow, white. The remaster draws it over the member's card portrait and over the hit monster's rank picture (one picture per rank) [~].

sound_effects._note: The Amiga's sounds (FORMAT.md 7.2) [C] static s110: 0xb126(n) calls the music driver's start 0x1f52(t[n], t[n+1], t[n+2]), t = the long pointers at 0x23e1a (DATA), so a sound is three voice streams in the driver's format and cuts whatever plays. Offsets below are in the program file (DATA flat address + 0x6038); null = a 0 pointer, a silent voice; 33 (all null) is the driver's stop. Wired: 15 on each reward and combat flash and every melee 'hits!' line (0x1662c, 0x17eda), 18 on a melee miss (0x16682 / 0x17b28), 21 on the cast lines (s127: the party's 0x1620a; the monsters' Fireflash / Quickness / Strength / Protection / Mindblast / Fireball / Sleep lines and the lowered armour / attack lines, 0x17184 ... 0x17436); s158: 33 (the stop) before 'The monsters flee!' (0x15990, a line tag) and 'The party gets away!' (0x19c66, GameSession.PlaySound). Callers (not wired): 3 0x19da0, 6 0x10902 / 0x13938 / 0x1f5c8, 9 0x1dfe6 (defeat: a member not destroyed), 12 0x1f93c / 0x20308, 24 0x14a28, 36 0x111e0 / 0x11386, 39 0x18610, 42 0x1092c / 0x1d516, 45 0x1dde6 (the defeat's demon), 48 0x18132 (and the defeat: a member destroyed); 27 comes from the event word 0x240fa, 30 has no caller. s136: the dungeon / overworld sounds are wired from Core's P3Sounds (GameSession.PlaySound): 6 with a member's dungeon line (0x1f572), 12 the wall bump, 42 the Damage Report / special doors / op 9 / leftover ops 1-4 and 10, 3 op 7 / leftover op 8, 9 op 12, 27 op 14 (FORMAT.md 7.2). s140 (FS-UAE trace, capture_s140_p3_sounds.md): 36 has a sixth caller (a PC-relative call the s135 sweep missed): it plays before window 1's five 'Are you sure...?' / 'two months' confirm questions; s141: wired on the remaster's one such question, the guild Add's 'two months' (GameSession.AskConfirmQuestion).
